dedupe_keys.name: production of gathering spaces in post disaster recovery great east japan earthquake and tsunami 2011 four tohoku neighbourhoods

description: An open access article in City, Territory and Architecture (2023) that compares how gathering and public spaces were produced during recovery from the Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami of 2011. Four severely damaged neighbourhoods in Miyagi and Iwate prefectures are studied: Aoi in Higashimatsushima, Tamauranishi in Iwanuma, Machikata in Otsuchi and Shishiori in Kesennuma. The authors combine municipal documents, field visits, interviews and a questionnaire survey (2,076 forms distributed, 362 returned, 18 percent) and apply Arnstein's ladder of citizen participation and Lefebvre's production of space. Lessons: community-driven cases gave small, accessible, well connected open spaces, while government-led cases centred spaces near disaster public housing, with a wider range of leisure activities. Coverage: four sites; the initial data come from an earlier questionnaire report by Hokugo and others. Access: free full text under CC BY 4.0, no data file. Caveats: low response rates, 13 to 29 percent by site. It supports recovery planning and post-disaster public space design; related records are not yet linked.

name: Production of gathering spaces in post-disaster recovery, Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami 2011: four Tohoku neighbourhoods
outcomes: Community-driven recovery produced small, evenly spread and accessible gathering spaces linked to each other, whereas government-led recovery produced centralised spaces near disaster public housing with weak links between them.
provider: Kobe University Graduate School of Engineering (Yegane Ghezelloo, Akihiko Hokugo, Osamu Tsukihashi); journal City, Territory and Architecture

sources.note: Europe PMC full text: four study areas, 2,076 questionnaires distributed and 362 returned, 13-29% return by case, CC BY 4.0, data availability statement, findings on community-driven vs government-led

study_period: Recovery after the March 2011 event; article published 2023
